push_headlines: Oil slid on recovering Middle East exports: Brent -3.55% to $92.44 and WTI -3.21% to $85.72.
Asia fell on the Nvidia fallout: the Nikkei 225 -2.42% to 59,662.02 after Japan's GDP contracted; the Hang Seng +0.52% to 23,759.37.
Europe's five-day record run ended: the STOXX 600 -0.28% to 662.31 as AI worries hit tech.
on_notice: Nvidia reports Tuesday after Jensen Huang's exit as CEO, and the Nasdaq slid for a third straight day, so Nasdaq 100 futures may swing overnight.
Asian chipmakers took the brunt on Monday (SK Hynix -7.9%, Taiwan's Taiex -4.1%), so watch whether the selling extends Tuesday.
Oil has turned toward surplus: the IEA sees a fourth-quarter surplus above 1.7 million barrels a day as Hormuz flows recover.

asia.headline: Tokyo and Seoul fell as the Nvidia fallout extended into a second week.
asia.detail: The Nikkei 225 -2.42% to 59,662.02 after data showed Japan's economy contracted last quarter. In Seoul, SK Hynix -7.9% and Samsung Electronics -4.5% dragged the Kospi; Taiwan's Taiex -4.1% with TSMC -3.4%. No verified Kospi close was found.

china.headline: Hong Kong bucked the region as bargain hunters returned; no verified Shanghai close was found.
china.detail: The Hang Seng +0.52% to 23,759.37, snapping a three-session losing run as buyers stepped in at lower valuations. Searches returned no citable Shanghai Composite close for Monday, so no mainland level is quoted here.

europe.headline: The STOXX 600 slipped from record territory, ending a five-session winning run.
europe.detail: The STOXX 600 -0.28% to 662.31 as worries about the AI trade weighed on tech shares. No confirmed DAX or FTSE 100 close was found.

latam.headline: No Ibovespa close for Monday was found.
latam.detail: Searches returned no Rio Times or B3 report for Monday's session, so no Brazilian level is quoted here.

mideast.headline: Oil fell sharply as Middle East exports recovered and surplus forecasts grew.
mideast.detail: Brent -3.55% to $92.44 and WTI -3.21% to $85.72 in afternoon trade, per CNBC. The IEA expects a fourth-quarter supply surplus above 1.7 million barrels a day as Strait of Hormuz flows recover, and Goldman Sachs sees Brent averaging $88.00 in 2027.
